tests.name: Quick Knowledge Check
tests.description: 5 quick questions to test basic understanding of cell structure

questions.question: Which organelle is the site of photosynthesis in plant cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis.

questions.question: Animal cells have a cell wall made of cellulose.
questions.explanation: Animal cells do not have a cell wall. Only plant, fungal, and bacterial cells have cell walls.

questions.question: What is the function of ribosomes?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis in the cell.

questions.question: Name the organelle that controls the activities of the cell.
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains DNA and controls cell activities.

questions.question: A cell measures 0.05 mm under a microscope at ×400 magnification. What is the actual size of the cell in micrometres?

tests.name: Deep Dive Test
tests.description: 10 questions covering structure, function, and adaptations

questions.question: A student observes a cell with a cell membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes, and DNA free in the cytoplasm (no nucleus). What type of cell is it?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells (bacteria) have DNA free in cytoplasm (nucleoid), no membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.question: Match each organelle to its function:
questions.correctAnswer: Mitochondria → Aerobic respiration / ATP production; Ribosomes → Protein synthesis; Nucleus → Controls cell / contains DNA; Cell membrane → Controls movement in/out; Chloroplast → Photosynthesis; Vacuole → Storage / turgor pressure
questions.explanation: Each organelle has a specific function in the cell.

questions.question: Order these from smallest to largest: Ribosome, Mitochondria, Nucleus, Cell, Atom
Explain why palisade mesophyll cells are adapted for photosynthesis.
questions.correctAnswer: Many chloroplasts; tall shape packed together; thin cell walls; large vacuole pushes chloroplasts to edge; at top of leaf
questions.explanation: Palisade cells have many chloroplasts for light absorption, columnar shape for packing, thin walls for gas diffusion, large vacuole positioning chloroplasts near light.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the difference between rough and smooth ER?
options: Rough ER has ribosomes; makes proteins. Smooth ER has no ribosomes; makes lipids.
Rough ER has no ribosomes; makes lipids. Smooth ER has ribosomes; makes proteins.
Both have ribosomes but rough ER is larger.
Rough ER is in plants only; smooth ER is in animals only.
questions.explanation: Rough ER is studded with ribosomes (protein synthesis). Smooth ER lacks ribosomes (lipid/steroid synthesis).

tests.description: Timed test with exam-style questions including 6-marker

questions.question: What is the magnification if a 20 μm cell appears as 10 mm?

options.question: Compare the structure of a typical plant cell and a typical animal cell. Include at least 4 differences.
options.correctAnswer: Plant: cell wall (cellulose), chloroplasts, large permanent vacuole, plasmodesmata. Animal: no cell wall, no chloroplasts, small/no vacuoles, centrioles, lysosomes.
options.explanation: Key differences: cell wall, chloroplasts, vacuole size, plasmodesmata vs centrioles/lysosomes.
